about.title: About
about.privacyBody: This app doesn't collect any personal information. Tournament records and settings are stored only on this device, and the app never connects to the internet.
about.noticeBody: This app is a scorekeeping tool. It can't be used for real-money gambling.
about.rulesBody: Tournament procedures follow rules commonly used in live poker tournaments.

sections.title: What this app does
items: Keeps score in place of chips while you play a Texas Hold'em tournament with a real deck of cards.
Put one phone in the middle of the table and share it. The app doesn't deal cards, so you pick the winner on screen after the showdown.

sections.title: Starting a tournament
items: Tap New tournament, choose the blind structure, starting stack and players, then start.
Pick one of three preset blind structures, or edit any level yourself.

sections.title: Playing a hand
items: Tap Deal Hand #1. The small blind, big blind and big blind ante are posted automatically.
The highlighted seat is the player to act. Enter what they declare: Fold, Check, Call, Bet or Raise.
Set a bet or raise with the Min, ½ Pot, Pot and All-in buttons, the slider, or by typing an amount. Amounts that aren't allowed can't be entered.
When the betting round is complete, the app moves to the next street. The card outlines in the middle show how many board cards should be face up.

sections.title: Showdown
items: If the hand goes to showdown, choose the winner of each pot and tap Confirm winners.
For a split pot, select every player who ties and the pot is divided evenly. Side pots are calculated for you.

sections.title: Fixing mistakes
items: Tap Undo to step back one action at a time (up to 50). If you close the app, you can resume where you left off.

sections.title: Blinds and the clock
items: The clock starts with the first hand and moves to the next level when time runs out. New blinds take effect from the next hand.
A sound and a banner announce each new level. You can turn the sound off in Settings.

sections.title: Eliminations, re-entry and late registration
items: Players who run out of chips are eliminated. While registration is open, re-entries and late registrations can be made from Standings.

sections.title: Key rules
items: Big blind ante: the player in the big blind posts the ante for the whole table.
Minimum raise: a raise must be at least as large as the previous bet or raise in that round.
An all-in for less than a full raise does not reopen the betting to players who have already acted.
When betting is over with a player all-in, all hands are turned face up before the rest of the board is dealt.
In a split pot, an odd chip goes to the winner closest to the left of the button.
Heads-up, the button posts the small blind and acts first before the flop.
